kelly (People Ops): Quick clarification on handback SLA: managers should aim to complete handbacks within 48 hours of receiving the calibrated packet. If you expect a delay >24 hours, please file a brief delay notice in this thread with ETA. :alarm_clock:

omar (Eng Manager): For distributed teams, is it acceptable to batch handbacks (do all at once) or should we do per-person as we finish?

kelly (People Ops): Both are okay. Best practice: if you batch, mark the ETA and include a short note per person about who will receive feedback first to avoid confusion. The SLA still applies to the batch completion time.

violet (People Ops): Also important: handbacks must include the calibration summary line and next-step bullets (2-3) for growth. The template is in Review Console > Manager Templates. Missing template lines will trigger a triage flag.

raja (Manager): If my manager is OOO and I delegate, does that pause the 48-hour SLA?

kelly (People Ops): Delegation does not pause the SLA. Use the handoff form to delegate; the delegate then inherits the remaining SLA window. If no delegate is registered, reach out to People Ops and we can extend on a case-by-case basis.

intake-bot: reminder: handback template missing for 3 receipts in your queue (uids: r-44a, r-77b, r-88c)  flagged at 2026-08-12T02:45:10Z (UTC)

omar (Eng Manager): One edge case: interactive handbacks (1:1 call) sometimes run over the allotted time. If the call spills into the next day and ratings need minor clarification, do we update the packet post-call?

violet (People Ops): Minor clarifications (typo fixes, wording) are fine post-call with an "UPDATED_POST_HANDBACK" line and timestamp. Any rating edits after handback still require appeals/exception flow.

raja (Manager): Thanks. I'll post an ETA for my team now — running a few 1:1s tomorrow morning so expect batch completion by 2026-08-13T16:00:00Z (UTC).

kelly (People Ops): Perfect — thanks for the heads-up. We'll note the ETA and skip triage for your receipts until then. :white_check_mark:
